algorithm_name: IA-VFS
algorithm_type: integration-aware deep learning super-resolution with streamline-based loss
application_context: 3D vector fields for scientific visualization where streamline structure is an important downstream analysis target and seed placement should emphasize representative flow features.
application_goal: Improve 3D vector-field super-resolution so that integrated streamlines from the upsampled field more closely match ground truth streamlines.

evidence.quote: To this end, we consider seeding and integration length... To capture flow features, we use the entropy-based seeding technique of Xu et al. [XLS10]. We normalize the resulting entropy scalar field and treat it as a probability distribution from which to sample positions.
In order to not starve low-entropy regions of the flow field, we modify the distribution to interpolate between a uniform distribution, one that is a function of the entropy field.
While training, for all the experiments we used a subsampling factor r = 4, batch size of 1 and 2,000 streamlines within a batch to form the loss function (LS).
a more spread out selection of seed points in and around high entropy regions with α = -0.01 gives us the best ALP value and with acceptable PSNR.
We found that a λ = 0.3 provides a good balance between PSNR and ALP.
We found that model trained on streamline length of 350 provides good generalization when evaluated across different streamline lengths.

integration_direction: Not explicitly stated.
limitations_or_notes: Training directly with the combined loss from scratch was challenging; the model was first pretrained with content loss and then fine-tuned. The method uses a 3D volumetric CNN and differentiable integration with trilinear interpolation.
paper_title: Integration-Aware Vector Field Super Resolution
parameter_reasoning: The entropy-based distribution is intended to capture important flow features, while interpolation with a uniform distribution ensures low-entropy regions are not ignored. The authors report alpha = -0.01 gives the best ALP with acceptable PSNR, lambda = 0.3 provides a good balance, and training on length 350 generalizes well.

application_context: 2D stationary vector fields defined on a regular grid, where evenly spaced streamline placement is needed and long streamlines are preferred while maintaining control over density.

evidence.quote: Streamline integration starts from multiple randomly generated seed points located near previously-created streamlines. evidence.quote: This paper presents an Interactive View-Driven Evenly Spaced Streamline placement algorithm (IVDESS) for 3D explorative visualization of large complex planar or curved surface flows.

algorithm_name: 3D particle tracing
application_context: 4D Flow MRI of left atrial systolic vortical flow in healthy controls and patients with mitral valve regurgitation after atrioventricular septal defect correction, where the goal is to determine the source of organized intra-atrial flow.
application_goal: To identify the origin of the left atrial vortical flow and quantify how much of the vortical region originates from the left and right pulmonary veins.
data_dimension: 3D flow field from whole-heart 4D Flow MRI

evidence.quote: At end-systole the vortical flow was assessed by manually segmenting the volume of circular flow in the left atrium based on streamline visualization in a stack of slices parallel to the 4-chamber view. 3D-particle tracing was applied in reverse time order, using the defined volume as seeding, to trace back the seed points and quantify the number of particles originating from the left and right pulmonary veins (LPV and RPV).

Tracing revealed a dominating contribution to the vortical volume originating from the LPV (41±14%), a smaller part from the RPV (17±12%) and a residual part of particles present inside the atrium at the start of systole (42±15%).

Whole-heart 4D Flow MRI was performed on a 3T MR scanner with free breathing, three-directional velocity encoding of 150cm/s in all directions, spatial resolution 2.3×2.3×3.0-4.2mm3 and 30 phases reconstructed over one cardiac cycle.

integration_direction: Reverse time order / backward tracing
limitations_or_notes: The paper describes a manually segmented seed volume and backward particle tracing, but does not specify seed count, seed spacing, or explicit streamline termination criteria beyond tracing back the seed points. In patients, the residual category may include particles already in the atrium at systole or coming from ventricular regurgitation.

evidence.quote: We present an Advanced Evenly-Spaced Streamline (ADVESS) placement algorithm for fast, high-quality, and robust layout of flow lines.
We propose an improved seeding strategy that prioritizes topological seeding and favors long streamlines.
We employ two queues, a primary queue and a secondary queue. The primary queue serves as the major seed provider where initial topological seeds are assigned a highest weight.
Our ADVESS algorithm employs adaptive distance control based on the local flow variance.
We propose a fast effective loop detection strategy, which is robust due to high accuracy guaranteed through an RK4-ASSEC integrator.
Placements generated by our algorithm are better than those by Jobard and Lefer’s algorithm, and are comparable with those by Mebarki et al.’s algorithm in quality...

integration_direction: Both directions are used for streamline advection; loop detection logic accounts for positive and negative advection.
limitations_or_notes: The authors note an inherent tradeoff between strict uniformity and continuity/long streamlines; adaptive distance control helps reduce cavities but minScale should not be too small or global uniformity may be affected. Loop detection is described as robust but less accurate than fully general closed-streamline detectors.

evidence.quote: we present a coherent and feature-aware streamline generation algorithm by employing a feature-guided streamline seeding technique and a coherent streamline placing scheme.

Our approach employs a two stage seeding scheme: prior to optimizing the seeding positions by means of a deformation-driven algorithm, seeds are initialized subject to the critical features implied in a feature map.
The feature map is computed for each frame with critical points or the Finite-Time Lyapunov Exponent (FTLE) approach.
Subsequently, we distribute a set of seeds randomly in the region with valid masks by means of the Poisson Disk algorithm[31].
the threshold in our framework is not a constant over the entire domain, but changes with respect to the importance map. This threshold is lower in relatively important regions than other regions.
Figure 6 shows this process. ... The minimal distance is 3.0 pixels.
our approach can simultaneously preserve the temporal coherence by correlating the streamlines over time.

limitations_or_notes: May produce non-uniform spacing and visual clutter if features are uniformly and densely distributed; GPU acceleration is suggested to improve performance, especially in streamline correlation. The approach relies on feature identification via critical points or FTLE.

algorithm_name: Parallel Vectors feature extraction with RAA-guided octree/quadtree seed refinement and Newton-Raphson refinement
application_context: Higher-order, piecewise analytical cell-based data from discontinuous Galerkin simulations where line-type features must be seeded robustly despite cell-boundary discontinuities and higher-order polynomials.
application_goal: Extract line-type PV features from higher-order data accurately and efficiently while preserving bounds on existence, position, and topology.

evidence.quote: First, seed points on the feature lines are placed by evaluating the inclusion form of the PV criterion with reduced affine arithmetic. Second, a feature flow field is derived from the higher-order PV expression where the features can be extracted as streamlines starting at the seeds.

Our algorithm for PV feature extraction is composed of two stages. The seed extraction stage executes octree and quadtree-based adaptive subdivison followed by Newton iterations to accurately locate seeds.
If 0 ∈ ŵ(x̂, ŷ, ẑ) for the current octree cell, it potentially contains features and must be further subdivided.

The point p is considered as a seed if it has converged within the current quadtree cell limits after the execution of a maximum number of Newton iterations Nq. For all our experiments, Nq = 25 and the convergence thresholds |wx| ≤ 10−3, |wy| ≤ 10−3, and |wz| ≤ 10−3 worked well.

Our feature tracing method consists of a predictor-corrector scheme using a 4th-order Runge-Kutta scheme with fixed step size s. For all our experiments, we used s = 10−3 ... and three corrector moves per predictor move.

The parameter εF allows us to extract feature lines at different levels of the octree. Smaller values for εF capture smaller features at the cost of decreased performance and increased memory consumption.

integration_direction: Not explicitly stated as forward/backward; feature tracing follows streamlines of the feature flow field from seeds.
limitations_or_notes: The approach is designed for higher-order cell data and explicitly notes that feature integration across multiple cells is not feasible because of discontinuities and error buildup, so tracing is done separately per cell. The paper also notes that short-feature filtering was not usable for the DG results because boundary discontinuities disrupt correspondence across adjacent cells. Baseline methods such as Theisel et al. are discussed only for comparison; they are not the proposed strategy.

parameter_reasoning: εF sets the smallest feature scale that the octree is guaranteed to resolve; εS controls whether multiple intersections on a face are treated as separate seeds or merged. Newton iterations and convergence thresholds determine whether a candidate quadtree cell center is refined into an actual seed. The tracing parameters (s, corrector moves, batch size) are implementation choices for stable streamline extraction from the feature flow field.
